Structure of the recorded ancestral recombination graph (ARG)

Source: R/arg.R
arg_summary.Rd

Whole-genealogy summary: how many local trees and edges, how deep it goes, and – the key diagnostic for a forward run – how many ROOTS each local tree has. A fully coalesced genealogy has one root; this model seeds independent founder lineages, so the expected result is a forest with roughly one root per surviving founder lineage.

Usage

arg_summary(run, ids = NULL)

Arguments

run

a run: a vivax_run (from run_sim() or load_run()) or the path of a run directory.

ids

optional pedigree ids to restrict to (default: all recorded genomes); ids that are not genomes in the tree sequence are left out, and none being one is an error.

Value

a one-row data.table: num_trees, num_nodes, num_edges, num_samples, seq_length_mb, roots_min/roots_median/roots_max, pct_trees_coalesced, max_root_time (ticks before the end of the run). A run that recorded no genome, such as one that never started, gives the tree sequence's counts, no samples, 0 roots, and NA for pct_trees_coalesced and max_root_time.

Python

The IBD and ARG functions read a run's tree sequence with Python's tskit, through the reticulate package. Either of two routes works. Automatic: with no Python chosen, reticulate sets up its own environment with tskit (>= 1.0) and numpy the first time one of these functions runs; this needs internet once. Your own Python: set RETICULATE_PYTHON to a Python that has those modules (in ~/.Renviron to keep it) before the first such call of a session. A function that cannot reach them stops with an error of class malariafwd_no_python that says what to do, and check_setup() reports what is found.

Examples

arg_summary(example_run())
#>    num_trees num_nodes num_edges num_samples seq_length_mb roots_min
#>        <int>     <int>     <int>       <int>         <num>     <int>
#> 1:      4124      1679     12850        1679      24.21467        33
#>    roots_median roots_max pct_trees_coalesced max_root_time
#>           <num>     <int>               <num>         <num>
#> 1:           33        33                   0           399
